headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.72 (95% CI: 0.55–0.92), suggesting that Vitamin B1 is associated with a lower risk of renal cell carcinoma. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.

studies.Population: Population-based US Kidney Cancer Study participants in Detroit and Chicago
studies.comparison_type: lowest vs highest quartile (<=1.4 vs >2.2 mg/day)

sample_size.excerpt: 1142 EA and AA RCC cases and 1154 frequency‐matched controls were enrolled in a population‐based case‐control study between 2002 and 2007.
sample_size.location: Methods, Study population, paragraph 2; total_n derived from reported group counts 1142 + 1154 = 2296

cases.excerpt: Sociodemographic and baseline health characteristics and nutrient intake levels of 1142 cases and 1154 controls in the eligible study population are presented by race in Table 1 . Compared to controls, cases were more likely to report a lower education level, smoke, have a higher BMI and family history of RCC, and diagnosed with hypertension.

comparison.excerpt: the three lower quartiles were each compared to the highest quartile

design.excerpt: The US Kidney Cancer Study is a population‐based case‐control study designed to examine racial disparities between AA and EA in RCC risk.

continent.excerpt: The study was conducted in the metropolitan areas of Detroit (Wayne, Oakland, and Macomb counties), Michigan and Chicago (Cook County), Illinois.

ethnicity.excerpt: Eligible cases were EA and AA men and women between the ages of 20 and 79 years with newly diagnosed RCC.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary micronutrient intake was derived from an interviewer-administered diet history questionnaire.

gender.excerpt: Eligible cases were EA and AA men and women between the ages of 20 and 79 years with newly diagnosed RCC.

smoking_status.excerpt: Adjusted models included variables for: region (Detroit, Chicago), sex (male, female), race (White, African American), age (20‐44, 45‐54, 55‐64, 65‐74, 75+), education (<12 years, high school graduate, some college, 4+ years of college), smoking history (never, occasional/unknown, former, current), BMI (<25, 25‐30, 30‐<35, 35+_kg/m 2 ), RCC family history (none with cancer, unknown if diagnosed with cancer, diagnosed with other type of cancer, diagnosed with kidney cancer), and TDCI (continuous variable).
